title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Strata and common-area cleaning
audience: Owners of strata and common-area cleaning businesses who want repeat contracts and referrals from the strata managers, committees and building managers they already serve.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask at the moment the client is most satisfied
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the client has confirmed that the result is right, usually at sign-off or when the invoice is paid. For a strata contract, that is often after a full quarter of visits, when the manager has seen the standard hold. The AMA says timing depends on the type of product, and that experience goods need more evaluation time than search goods (AMA, 10 January 2023). In one Baylor Keller Center experiment, reviews rose from 1.32 per cent of customers with no reminder to 2.16 per cent with a late reminder (1 June 2024). Ask the manager or committee once, in one sentence, and make it easy to decline. Sending a review link or QR code is allowed, and Google provides one (Google Business Profile Help). Do not write or invent reviews. Asking only satisfied clients is called review gating, which Podium says Google treats as a violation (2 May 2022, a vendor source). The ACCC says incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (15 July 2026). Residents are private people, so ask them for a review only through the manager, and only if they agree. Google also bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews.

instruction.heading: Offer the next service before the client leaves
instruction.body: Repeat work is one of the most dependable sources of growth for a small service business. At sign-off, propose the next step with a date: a deep clean after the annual general meeting, a carpet clean for the common corridors, a window clean for the lift lobby, or a fortnightly service added to the weekly clean. Put the scope, the interval and the price approach in writing. Ask who approves spend before you make the offer, because a committee often has its own approval process, and confirm the approval before you change the schedule. If the written offer goes by email, check the Spam Act first. ACMA's guidance indicates that inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase, and a generic business inbox carries risk because consent must be provable. If a recurring contract renews automatically, a law-firm summary says renewal notices and online cancellation rules take effect on 1 July 2027 (McCullough, 3 July 2026), so set out the renewal and cancellation terms now.

instruction.heading: Check in at the interval that suits the service
instruction.body: Schedule a check-in after a period that suits the work. For a clean, a suggested starting point is about ninety days, which is a choice to test, not a benchmark. For a strata contract, a quarterly review with the manager may suit better, timed to the committee's meeting cycle. The check asks whether the standard still holds, whether anything has changed and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short, record what the manager said, and close the loop with a reply. A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023), so keep check-ins factual and check each one against the Spam Act. ACMA's summary (read 2026-11-04) does not say whether one-to-one messages are covered, so check that point before you send.

instruction.heading: Re-contact previous clients before their busy periods
instruction.body: Many strata needs follow the calendar: a committee's annual general meeting, a pre-summer clean of the common areas, a gutter or car park clean before the wet season, or a clean before a building inspection. Plan a short message to the manager a few weeks before each period. Offer the slots you can actually deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. Do not use the message to pressure anyone, and do not message individual lot owners with an offer, because they are not the buyer and their contact details are personal information. ACMA's guidance says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days, so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it and stop sending to that client.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the referrer knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide what you will offer, such as a credit on the next service or a small thank-you, and write down the condition for payment, which is normally that the referred building has signed and its first invoice is paid. Research on referral programmes found that stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals across seven studies (Xu, Yu and Tu, 2023), so say what the reward is in the invitation. Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 11 May 2017, an older source). In Victoria, the Owners Corporations Act 2006 index lists a manager's duty to disclose commission or other benefits (section 122B), and a manager's duty to disclose a beneficial relationship with a supplier (section 122A), so check both before offering a reward to a manager. The Act text was not read. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so the tax and contract effect of any reward is unconfirmed.

procedure: After each job is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-service offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm the committee's approval route.
Schedule the check-in for the interval that suits the contract, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message for each committee period in the calendar, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred job is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner completes the first quarter of weekly common-area cleans for a 24-lot building. The strata manager says she will recommend the cleaner to the manager of a neighbouring building. The cleaner wants to offer a credit on her next invoice if the neighbouring building signs.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should she do before the referral is made, and what should she avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: She writes down the reward terms before any referral happens: the credit, the condition that the neighbouring building signs and its first invoice is paid, and when the credit will be applied. She asks the strata manager to pass on the other manager's details, and she contacts that manager only if they agree. She does not promise a reward she has not written down. Because the referrer is a strata manager in Victoria, she checks the disclosure duties on commissions and benefits (sections 122A and 122B of the Owners Corporations Act 2006, index only) before offering anything. If she is unsure of the tax or contract effect of a credit, she confirms it with an adviser. She takes on only the work her licence and insurance cover.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of committee meeting and seasonal re-contact dates
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has confirmed the result.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, once the manager has confirmed the standard is being met.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a building's name, a lot owner's name, a site photo or a review without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, including site photos, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or messaging individual lot owners with an offer.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour each opt-out within five working days at most, and send offers only to the manager or committee.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a building's name, a lot owner's name, a site photo, a review or a property detail needs the consent of the person concerned for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, owners' and residents' details are personal information. Its coverage of small business is not confirmed in the research file, and privacy rules for using owners' details from a strata roll were not checked, so do not use those details for marketing.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content (15 July 2026). In Victoria, check the owners corporation manager's disclosure duties (Owners Corporations Act 2006, sections 122A and 122B, index only) before offering any reward to a manager. In NSW, the strata rules were not read for this lesson.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder, and ACMA has been enforcing this area, so check each message before sending.

A referral does not extend the licence or authority of the business that accepts the work. Accept only the work your licence and insurance cover, in the state where the work is done. Licence rules differ between states, so check the rules for each state you work in. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the manager or committee before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and committee confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next service in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a manager for a review or referral?
options: Before the first visit, so the committee feels committed
After the manager has confirmed the result is right
Only when a resident has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A strata manager wants to publish a review with the building's name and a photo of the lobby you cleaned. What do you need?
options: Their consent for the name and photo you plan to publish, and the building's consent where it applies
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred building books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for the client?
options: At the end of each job, with a date

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017 (older than 2022). Supports: the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: a reminder that promotes a service can be commercial.

Owners Corporations Act 2006 (Vic), table of provisions, AustLII, https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/vic/consol_act/oca2006260/index.html, undated. Index only; sections 122A and 122B read as index entries, not as Act text.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-04. Supports: unsubscribe within five working days; inferred consent is narrow; consent must be provable.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option under the Spam Act 2003, which the page says sets out responsibilities under Australian law. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
